You are acting as the "architect" agent: The primary Actor for an Epic's whole interactive conversation — owns overall plan and decomposition, clarifies scope, searches before building, decomposes work into scheduled PRDs via /develop, tracks them to completion, and verifies before calling anything done. Never implements a PRD itself — that's dev-lead's job, one PRD at a time, headless. Task-type framing is the Epic's Mission tag's job, not this persona's.

Work concisely: lead with the answer or the result, skip preamble, and don't recap what you just did unless asked. Verify before claiming something is done — run the check, read the file back, or show the actual output; don't assert success from what "should" have happened. Search the existing code/config for a pattern or utility to reuse before writing something new. Ask only when something is genuinely ambiguous and would cost real rework to guess wrong — don't ask permission for the obvious next step.

Grounding: System (CLAUDE.md, settings.json, agents/architect.md) · Project (CLAUDE.md, mcp servers · 5, Project brief) · Local (working tree, open Terminal tabs · 1, other Epics · 76)

You are in an open-ended discussion. The goal is a decision or shared understanding, not a code change — do not start editing files unless the human explicitly asks you to after the discussion lands somewhere.

Goal: Settings Home

The Settings Left Navigation contains a lot of configurations that are not clear if they are properaly applied or not. It is time to auit carefully and clean up the configursation
(1) Are they trully global change that effects multiple sessions or projects? 
(2) Is Settings the only place for this, lots of areas have more dedicate and indepenet left-navs. The entire Home-Landing page and the 2nd left-navigation menu are only Settings themself. We should stronly consider moving things out of settings
(3) Settings that do not have at least one consumer or rffeence shold also be deleted, they are duds!

## Audit: what's actually in "Settings"

First, a framing correction that changes the whole cleanup — **"Settings" is three unrelated populations wearing one label.**

| | What it is | Who consumes it | Can this app verify it applied? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | `settings.json` — 60 keys, Guided/Tree/Raw, 3 file scopes (`SETTINGS_SCOPES`) | the **`claude` CLI**, re-read from disk on every launch | **No.** Fire-and-forget file edit |
| **B** | `Telemetry` + `Session Manager` view tabs — `otel.json`, `rawSessionModel` localStorage | **this app** | Yes |
| **C** | 10 other app-owned pref stores | this app | Yes — but **none are in Settings** |

Your instinct that "the Configure nav is only Settings" is literally true for 6 of its 11 items. It is *not* true of the Home landing page — `Home.tsx` is billing/projects/queue/sessions/agents, no config.

---

### (1) Are they truly global?

**Population A: yes, and more global than the UI implies.** Per CLAUDE.md's own substrate rule, a Project-scope edit changes every current and future Epic in that project; User scope changes every Epic on the machine. That's fine — but three groups are *scope-mislabeled*:

- **`Interface`** (`spinnerTipsEnabled`, `spinnerVerbs`, `terminalProgressBarEnabled`, `showTurnDuration`, `statusLine`) governs the CLI's **interactive TUI**. It applies in a Terminal PTY view and is **inert in Chat and every scheduler job** (`-p --output-format stream-json`). Same file, two different realities depending on which view of the same Epic you're in.
- **`Model & Reasoning`** — already correctly demoted to advanced, but the demotion is half-done: `model` still sits in **Essentials** while the Agent persona's `model` beats it. You now have **three** model defaults in three screens: settings.json `model`, persona frontmatter (`AgentLibrary`), and `rawSessionModel` localStorage (`SettingsAppPrefs`).
- **`permissions`** — see below; it's not global, it's *nothing*.

**Population C: they're global too, they just have no home.** `app-prefs.json`, `chat-prefs.json`, `epics-prefs.json`, `projects-prefs.json`, `workbench-layout.json`, `voice.json`, `scheduler-machine.json`, session slots, `history-rollup`, `provenance.json`. `openToHomeOnLaunch` — a pure app preference — is buried in a section of the **Scheduler** tab.

### The load-bearing finding: Permissions is inert

Every single `claude` process this app launches passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions`:

`presets.ts:63` (all Terminal presets) · `chatRunner.cjs:538` · `scheduler.cjs:2506, 2858` · `runClaudeP.cjs:30` · `docEdit.cjs:95` · `supervisor.cjs:216` · `SimpleShell.tsx`

So the `permissions` key has **zero effect on any session started from this cockpit**. It only matters for a `claude` you launch yourself in a terminal outside the app. Yet it currently occupies: a whole Configure nav destination (`Permissions.tsx`), a slot in Settings' Essentials group, *and* a card in `GlobalControlsSection` that cheerfully reports **"N rule(s) configured"**. That card is the clearest instance of exactly what you're describing — a config surface that reads as applied and isn't.

### (2) Is Settings the only place? No — several things are rendered three times

`hooks`, `mcp`, `plugins`, `permissions` are each editable from **three** entry points over **one** file:

1. their own Configure nav destination,
2. a `SETTINGS_GROUPS` group inside Settings,
3. `GlobalControlsSection` — a card grid of *exactly* `Settings / Permissions / Hooks / MCP Servers / System Prompt / Skills`, i.e. a verbatim third copy of the Configure nav — which lives **inside the Scheduler tab**, not in Settings.

`GlobalControlsSection` is the clearest delete candidate on the page: pure duplication, wrong parent, and it's the surface printing the misleading permission count.

### (3) Duds

I ran the declared-vs-schema diff. **Zero true duds in Population A** — all 60 keys in `SETTINGS_GROUPS` exist in the bundled schemastore schema. Four schema keys are *ungrouped* and silently land in "Other":

`editorMode` · `skillOverrides` · `disableAgentView` · `disableRemoteControl`

Two real dead things elsewhere:
- **`disableRemoteControl` / `web-remote.json`** — `web-remote.json` sits in `~/.claude/session-manager/`, but `webRemote.cjs`, `WebRemote.tsx` and all three web-remote test files are **deleted in your working tree**. Dead state + a nav hint in CLAUDE.md still describing the feature.
- **`SessionManagerConfig.tsx`** isn't a dud but is unreachable as a destination — it's only mounted at `Scheduler.tsx:295`. It is, in substance, the "Settings Home" you're asking for, hidden in the wrong tab.

---

## Recommended target shape

**Settings becomes exactly one thing: the `claude` CLI's `settings.json`, three scopes, Guided/Tree/Raw.** Nothing else.

1. **Move `Telemetry` and `Session Manager` view-tabs OUT of Settings.** They are not `settings.json` and their presence is what makes the tab feel like a junk drawer.
2. **Promote `SessionManagerConfig` to a real Configure destination — "Session Manager"** — and make it own every Population-C pref: `openToHomeOnLaunch`, raw-session model, chat verbosity default, session slots, OTEL/telemetry, scheduler machine policy. That's your Settings Home.
3. **Delete `GlobalControlsSection`.** Third copy, wrong parent, misleading counts.
4. **Add an "applies to" badge per settings group** — `All sessions` / `Terminal only` / `Not applied — bypassed by --dangerously-skip-permissions`. This is the single highest-value change for "not clear if properly applied," and it's cheap: the data is static per group.
5. **Finish the model consolidation** — move `model` out of Essentials into the advanced Model group, and point Essentials at Agent Library, so there's one visible answer to "what model runs."
6. **Group the four orphan keys** (`editorMode` → Interface, `skillOverrides` → a Skills group, `disableAgentView`/`disableRemoteControl` → Advanced) so "Other" stays empty as a drift signal.
7. **Sweep the web-remote remnants** — `web-remote.json` and the CLAUDE.md/nav references.

Two decisions I won't guess at, because they'd cost real rework either way:

(C) lets not manage permissions for now, we get instructions from use and bypass questions
Lets the config UX stay for now, we want to evolve it but we need to keep it all visiable

Decisions recorded. Reconciling the two — they're not in conflict, they answer different questions:

- **Permissions specifically → stop managing it.** Delete the management surface.
- **Everything else in the config UX → stays visible.** No collapsing of the six Configure destinations, no hiding behind "advanced". Evolve in place.

---

## Resolved: Permissions is retired as a managed surface

**Rationale of record:** every `claude` this app launches passes `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (`presets.ts:63`, `chatRunner.cjs:538`, `scheduler.cjs:2506/2858`, `runClaudeP.cjs:30`, `docEdit.cjs:95`, `supervisor.cjs:216`, `SimpleShell.tsx`). Gating is done by *instruction* — the Agent persona and the Tag's mission template — not by an allow/deny table. A permissions editor in this cockpit is a control panel wired to nothing.

**Blast radius** (measured, not estimated):

| Surface | File | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| Nav destination | `navGroups.ts:64`, `screenKeys.ts:30`, `LeftNav.tsx:20`, `screenComponents.tsx:55,104` | remove |
| The editor | `Permissions.tsx` (409 lines) + `Permissions.navface.test.tsx` | delete |
| Slash route | `slashCommand.ts:5` (`/permissions`) | remove |
| Global Controls card | `GlobalControlsSection.tsx:129` — the "N rule(s) configured" claim | remove card (section itself already slated for deletion as a 3rd copy of the nav) |
| Icon | `AlmanacIcon.tsx:75` `'permissions'` | drops to unused once the nav row goes |
| Learning copy | `learningContent.ts:164,183` — including a line that explicitly advertises "the dedicated Permissions tab" | rewrite to state permissions are bypassed |
| **Catalog presets** | `catalog.ts:256` `CATALOG_PERMS_PRESETS` → applied by `Library.tsx:587` | **a third permission-writing surface** — must go with it, or Library keeps writing rules nothing reads |

**What deliberately stays visible**, consistent with your second answer: the `permissions` **key itself** in `SETTINGS_GROUPS.essentials` (`settingsGroups.ts:29`). It's a real key in a real file that a `claude` you launch outside this app will honor. It stays editable in Guided/Tree/Raw — it just loses its dedicated cockpit and gains a *"not applied to sessions started here"* label. Deleting the management UI ≠ hiding the file's contents.

## Rest of the audit, re-scoped to "keep it all visible, evolve in place"

Dropped (they were collapse/hide moves, against your call): merging the six Configure destinations into Settings groups; demoting anything behind "advanced".

Still live, all additive:

1. **"Applies to" badge per settings group** — `All sessions` / `Terminal only` / `Not applied`. Highest value for your "not clear if properly applied" complaint, and it *adds* visibility rather than removing it. `Interface` (`spinnerTipsEnabled`, `spinnerVerbs`, `terminalProgressBarEnabled`, `showTurnDuration`, `statusLine`) is `Terminal only` — inert in Chat and every scheduler job, which run `-p --output-format stream-json`.
2. **Promote `SessionManagerConfig` to a real "Session Manager" Configure destination.** It's currently only reachable at `Scheduler.tsx:295`. This is the "Settings Home" you asked for, and it's a visibility *gain*: `openToHomeOnLaunch`, session slots, telemetry, raw-session model, chat verbosity default, scheduler machine policy are today spread across 10+ pref files with no single owner.
3. **Delete `GlobalControlsSection`** — verbatim third copy of the Configure nav, living inside the Scheduler tab. Removing a duplicate doesn't reduce what's visible.
4. **One model answer.** Three defaults exist right now: `settings.json` `model`, persona frontmatter (Agent Library, wins), `rawSessionModel` localStorage. Keep all three editable; make Settings' `model` state that the persona overrides it.
5. **Group the four orphan keys** so "Other" stays empty as a drift alarm: `editorMode` → Interface, `skillOverrides` → new Skills group, `disableAgentView` + `disableRemoteControl` → Advanced.
6. **Sweep web-remote remnants** — `~/.claude/session-manager/web-remote.json` persists while `webRemote.cjs`, `WebRemote.tsx` and three test files are deleted in your working tree.

No duds found in the settings.json population itself: all 60 keys in `SETTINGS_GROUPS` verified present in the bundled schemastore schema, zero orphans.

---

**Summary:** Audited all three Settings populations against real consumers. Confirmed Permissions is inert app-wide and mapped its 7-surface blast radius including a third writer (`Library.tsx` catalog presets) that would otherwise be orphaned. Recorded your two decisions — retire Permissions management, keep the rest of the config UX visible and evolve in place — and re-scoped the remaining six recommendations to be additive-only. Nothing was edited; this stays a discussion until you say to build it.

Two notes, since neither was mine to decide:

1. **These changes were already in the working tree when this session started** — they're the Web Remote removal continuing `4fcc209`/`1603b12`, not output of this Epic. I made no source edits; the Settings audit is still a discussion with nothing built.
2. **`~/.claude/session-manager/web-remote.json` still exists on disk** — the code is gone but its state file isn't. That's item 6 on the audit's remaining list and I left it alone since it's outside the repo.

The seven Settings-audit items (retire Permissions across its 7 surfaces incl. `Library.tsx`'s catalog presets, "applies to" badges, promote `SessionManagerConfig` to a real nav destination, delete `GlobalControlsSection`, one model answer, group the 4 orphan keys, sweep web-remote remnants) are decided but unbuilt — say the word and I'll decompose them into PRDs.
